task_instance: Given a JS file (input.js) containing a start-shorthand/end-shorthand block with '()=>' pseudo-code lines describing an isAdult(users) filter function, interpret the shorthand, implement production-quality JavaScript, remove all '()=>' lines, and verify the resulting function behaves correctly.
evidence: Created /tmp/claude-0/.../exec_fresh/github__awesome-copilot__quasi-coder/input.js containing a start-shorthand/end-shorthand block with three '()=>' lines describing an isAdult(users) function. Rewrote the file: removed all '()=>' shorthand lines and the markers, and implemented a JSDoc-documented isAdult(users) function with input validation (throws TypeError on non-array) and a filter over users with age > 18, exported via module.exports. Verified with `grep -n '()=>' input.js` returning no matches (shorthand fully removed), and by running a Node.js test script that called isAdult on a sample array of users (ages 10, 25, 18, 19, and one with no age field) — output `result: [{"age":25},{"age":19}]` and printed 'TEST PASSED', confirming correct behavior (age > 18 strictly, non-numeric age excluded).
